subject: SLO targets & POC schedule for ACME - hosted latency qualification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — SLO targets & proposed POC plan

Hi Sam / Lina,

Thanks again for the time today — good alignment on the workload and the production constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get a hosted POC running that validates end-to-end p95 / p99 targets against your real traffic pattern.

Key SLO asks you called out:
- p95 end-to-end (user request -> final token delivered): <= 120 ms (US-East primary)
- p99 end-to-end: <= 400 ms (US-East primary); EU-West is soft target but we'd like comparability
- Sustained throughput: ~120 qps for inference (text-generation API)
- Concurrency: 20 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled (chunked tokens)
- Streaming latency: initial token (first byte) < 80 ms; subsequent token latency budget not to exceed 15 ms per token on average

Current provider baseline you mentioned on the call: p95 ~ 210–230 ms, p99 ~ 850–950 ms end-to-end (including your network and app-side post-processing).

Proposed POC (hosted):
1) We will run a 48–72 hour end-to-end POC from US-East using a replay of a 1-hour sample trace you provided + synthetic bursts to validate tail behavior.
2) Redwood will provide a pre-configured test harness (we'll share the test plan and scripts) and a dedicated hosted instance with pinned model and quantization profile.
3) Acceptance criteria: sustained p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 400 ms for production-like request mix and concurrency pattern. If we miss p99, we will iterate on batching/kv-cache/quantization and re-run.

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO table), poc-testplan.md (test steps and scripts), redwood-hosted-benchmarks.pdf (representative numbers).

Next steps / asks from Acme:
- Confirm the 1-hour trace file we should replay (s3 link or attachment).
- Confirm preferred POC start window (we suggested Sep 8–10).
- Identify the EngOps contact who can open an IP allowlist entry for our test runner.

I can loop Ben (solutions) and Jonas (runtime lead) to coordinate the test harness and scheduling.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: slo-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), poc-testplan.md (markdown), redwood-hosted-benchmarks.pdf (pdf)

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SLO targets & proposed POC plan

Karthik —

Thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The p95 <= 120 ms is non-negotiable for the US-East region; EU-West can be relaxed to p95 <= 200 ms as long as user-facing latency is comparable.
- p99 <= 400 ms is our stretch but is material for the support SLA in the RFP. If hosted can demonstrate p99 consistently below 400 ms we can consider switching.
- When we quoted current provider numbers, that includes our app-layer post-processing (~20–30 ms) and a Cloudflare layer; so the raw inference portion is actually ~150–200 ms p99 in some peaks.

Concurrency note: 20 concurrent streaming sessions is an ongoing minimum requirement — some days we spike to 40 for short bursts. For the POC please include burst tests up to 60 concurrent streams for 5–10 minutes.

Trace: I uploaded a 1-hour anonymized sample to the shared Drive folder you listed (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-poc-docs). EngOps contact is engops@acmecorp.com — they will open the necessary allowlist.

POC window: Sep 8 (AM PT) or Sep 9 (AM PT) works for us. Please confirm which you prefer and what time.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Product — Conversational AI | Acme Corp

Karthik

Sam — appreciate the quick turnaround and for uploading the trace. Sep 8 AM PT is good for us; we propose a 2-hour window starting at 09:00 PT to run the live replay and an extended 24-hour soak starting immediately after to capture tail behavior.

Operational notes:
- We'll provision a dedicated hosted instance in US-East with pinned model and our recommended quantization profile. Jonas — please tune batching to prioritize tail latency (small token batches, dynamic KV cache).
- We will run bursts up to 60 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 minutes to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies.
- Acceptance criteria reminder: p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 400 ms (end-to-end). If we miss, we will run two remedial passes with adjusted kernel selection and caching.

Deliverables before POC:
- Updated poc-testplan.md (linked in Drive).
- Baseline dry-run numbers from Jonas (expected p95/p99 under synthetic traffic).
- Exec one-pager for Sam's leadership summarizing objectives and pass/fail criteria.

Sam — I'll send calendar invites for Sep 8 09:00–11:00 PT (live run) and a follow-up readout for Sep 10. If anything changes on your side, let us know.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
